answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it may transact, like a yarrow root that must take hold before it flowers. Forging ten thousand fake agents then means locking ten thousand stakes, so the cost of an attack rises faster than the profit from one double-spend. Honest agents recover their stake after a clean record, while a river of cheap throwaway identities dries up because each one must pay to enter and forfeits its deposit if it misbehaves. The ledger enforces the bond instead of any ivory tower.
